# **Programmable Gain Instrumentation Amplifier Linear-in-dB from 18 dB to 78 dB on IHP SG13CMOS5L with Hybrid Dual-Stage Coarse and Fine Gain Tune**

## *Chipalooza 2026*

## *Challenge \#2: IHP SG13CMOS5L*

1. # **Motivation**

Precision low-frequency sensor interfaces in mixed-signal SoCs require front-end amplifiers capable of measuring weak signals with high input impedance, low offset, and noise, while ensuring stability across varying conditions. This project aims to address these needs by developing a programmable instrumentation amplifier IP, offering flexibility in gain and operation to support diverse sensor applications without requiring custom redesigns. Beyond enhancing IP reusability and attractiveness for SoC designers, the project is driven by the necessity for an open-source, reproducible design flow that minimizes manual iteration and facilitates a streamlined path from specification to verified implementation.

2. # **Proposed IP Block**

The proposed IP block is a **Programmable Gain Instrumentation Amplifier for Precision & Low-Frequency Sensor Interfaces**, typically biosignals (EEG, ECG, EMG, EOG). This design is optimized for high-precision mixed-signal SoC environments where reliable measurement of small differential signals is critical. Target applications include biochemical sensing, battery monitoring, and precision instrumentation. The core value proposition of this IP lies in its reusability and configurability of its gain. By providing a flexible analog front-end with adjustable gains, the block allows SoC designers to support diverse sensor types and varying signal conditions without the need for custom hardware redesigns. This approach reduces time-to-market and enhances the utility of the IP across multiple product generations.

3. # **Architecture Overview**

![][image1]  
Fig 1\.  Top-level system

* The gain (in dB) follows a linear-in-dB gain levels and can be calculated as follows:

GdB,total=GdB,IA+GdB,coarse+GdB,fine+GdB,buffer

* GdB,IA constant on 18.06 dB  
  * GdB,coarse ranging from 0 dB to \+56.25 dB with \+3.75 dB/step  
  * GdB,fine ranging from 0 dB to \+3.69 dB with \+0.0581 dB/step  
  * GdB,buffer approximately 0 dB  
* A DC offset cancellation may be used, but current proposal doesn’t use it  
* There are two separate voltage domains: analog voltage sources (AVDD/AVSS) for most building blocks and digital voltage sources (DVDD/DVSS) only for 10-bit decoder

### **Instrumentation Amplifier (Initial Stage)**

The primary purpose of the Input Buffering Stage is to provide high input impedance (exceeding 1 G) to buffer the sensor signals, initiate Common-Mode Rejection Ratio (CMRR) performance, and establish an initial gain of 8x. The architectural choice for this stage utilizes two unity-gain voltage follower buffers driving a difference-amplifier subtractor, forming a two-op-amp instrumentation amplifier (IA). Interfacing with VINP, VINN, VCM, VBIAS, and AVDD/AVSS, the stage has a single-ended output to the PGA. The buffer stage can be seen from Fig 2\.  
![][image2]  
Fig 2\. Instrumentation Amplifier as Input Stage

### **Gain Switching Network**

The gain switching network consists of two hybrid stages:

* Coarse-gain stage

This stage utilized a single-ended operational amplifier with a switched-resistor feedback network. It serves as coarse-gain adjustment block with 4-bit digital control word (D0-D3) and gain range from 0 dB to \+56.25 dB with gain step of \+3.75 dB/logarithmic step size. Every switch uses a transmission gate and it will be controlled by a single decoder. Because there are 16 switches, a specific thermometer decoder that translates 4-to-16 (4-bit digital controls to control 16 switches) levels will be used in that single decoder. There are 17 resistors used in this stage. The architecture of this stage can be seen from Fig 3\.

![][image3]

Fig 3\. Coarse-gain stage (Stage 2\)

* Fine-gain stage

This stage also utilized a single-ended operational amplifier with R-2R resistor ladder network that serves a fine-gain stage. It uses 6-bit digital control word (D4-D9) with a gain range from 0 dB to 3.69 dB and a gain step of \+0.0586 dB, totalling all of the digital control signals to be 10-bit or 1024 levels. There are 15 resistors used in this stage. Every switch uses a transmission gate and it will be controlled by a single decoder. The control signals used for the 6-bit buffer & inverter array to control each switch in the single decoder. The architecture of this stage can be seen from Fig 4\.

![][image4] 

Fig 4\. Fine-gain stage (Stage 3\)

### **Output Buffer**

The output Buffer and driver stage is designed to provide a low-impedance output, suitable for driving off-chip loads such as ADC inputs or PCB traces. It is implemented as a unity-gain voltage follower. The buffer provides the final VOUT signal. The buffer circuit can be seen from Fig 5\.  
![][image5]  
Fig 5\. Output Buffer Stage

### **Bias Network**

The bias network serves to convert voltage references into a stable current reference IBIAS for all operational transconductance amplifiers (OTAs). It employs a V-to-I converter architecture consisting of a diode-connected MOSFET and transistors for reliable startup, followed by current-mirror replica biasing. The detailed architecture will be explored while designing.

### **Digital Decoder**

The Digital Control Logic acts as a decoder that translates the 10-bit gain control input into the specific switch-drive signals required by the gain switching network. The architecture is a static CMOS decoder utilizing pure combinational logic to produce non-overlapping ON/OFF signal pairs. This selection ensures zero static power consumption and high area efficiency. The logic interfaces between the digital control inputs (D0-D9) and the PGA switch control lines, operating on the DVDD/DVSS power domain.

4. # **I/O & Port List**

| Port Category | Label | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Analog Input | VINP | Positive differential analog input |
|  | VINN | Positive differential analog input |
| Analog Output | VOUT | Output of the amplifier (single-ended) |
| Power Supply | AVDD | Analog supply voltage |
|  | AVSS | Analog ground |
|  | DVDD | Digital supply voltage |
|  | DVSS | Digital ground |
| Bias and Reference | VCM | Common-mode reference input |
|  | VBIAS | BGR (1.2 V) (If on one die, this port can be removed) |
| Digital Control | D0-D9 | Digital control for gain |

6. # **Verification, Test Plan, and Available Tools**

### **Verification**

Each of these verification must be done on various gain configurations (G \= 8, 80, 800, 8000 V/V gain sweep)

List of Verifications:

* Bode Plot to visualize PM, GM, GBW, BW   
* CMRR vs frequency  
* CMRR monte carlo  
* PSRR vs frequency  
* PSRR monte carlo  
* Voltage noise density vs frequency (IRN expressed in nV/sqrt(Hz))  
* Gain mismatch and/or linearity sweep  
* Input bias current vs Temperature  
* Offset Voltage Temperature Drift monte carlo  
* Maximum Output Voltage vs Frequency  
* THD \+ Noise vs Frequency  
* Power consumption  
* Input Impedance  
* Dedicated gain switching verifications (transient response, repeatability, and check whether the gain actually achieved the said target)

### **Test Plan and Available Tools**

Silicon characterization:

| Verification | Simulation Tools (Pre-Silicon) | Silicon Test Equipment (Post-Silicon) |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Bode Plot (PM, GM, GBW, BW)** | Xschem, ngspice/Xyce (AC analysis), Python (NumPy/Matplotlib) | Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) or Frequency Response Analyzer, Oscilloscope |
| **CMRR vs Frequency** | Xschem, ngspice/Xyce (AC), Python | Differential Signal Generator, VNA/FRA, Oscilloscope |
| **CMRR Monte Carlo** | ngspice/Xyce Monte Carlo scripts (or custom Python automation) | Measure multiple fabricated chips (if we get more than one), statistical analysis in Python |
| **PSRR vs Frequency** | Xschem, ngspice/Xyce (AC), Python | Low-noise Programmable Power Supply, Function Generator (inject ripple), Oscilloscope/VNA |
| **PSRR Monte Carlo** | ngspice/Xyce Monte Carlo, Python | Multiple chips, programmable supply, statistical analysis |
| **Voltage Noise Density (Input-Referred Noise)** | ngspice Noise Analysis, Python FFT/integration | Low-Noise Preamplifier, Dynamic Signal Analyzer or Spectrum Analyzer, Shielded Test Fixture |
| **Gain Accuracy / Linearity Sweep** | ngspice DC/AC Sweep, Python | Precision SourceMeter (SMU), Precision DMM, Oscilloscope |
| **Input Bias Current vs Temperature** | ngspice Temperature Sweep | Temperature Chamber, Picoammeter or Electrometer, SMU |
| **Offset Voltage Temperature Drift (Monte Carlo)** | ngspice Monte Carlo \+ Temperature Sweep | Temperature Chamber, Nanovoltmeter / Precision DMM, Statistical analysis |
| **Maximum Output Voltage vs Frequency** | ngspice Transient \+ AC | Function Generator, Oscilloscope |
| **THD \+ Noise vs Frequency** | ngspice Transient \+ FFT, Python | Audio Analyzer (e.g., APx series) or Spectrum Analyzer \+ Low-Distortion Signal Generator |
| **Power Consumption** | ngspice Operating Point / DC Sweep | Precision Power Analyzer, SMU, Precision DMM |
| **Input Impedance** | ngspice AC Analysis | Impedance Analyzer or LCR Meter |
| **Gain Switching Verification** | ngspice Transient, Xyce, Python automation | Arbitrary Waveform Generator (AWG), Oscilloscope (high sample rate), Logic Analyzer (if digital control), SMU |

The detailed list of available verified test equipment model numbers will be provided as a separate attachment alongside designer CVs, per submission rules.
